newsitem.title: USA: Quaker posts $1.2 billion loss; chairman may leave.
newsitem.headline: Quaker posts $1.2 billion loss; chairman may leave.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co., posting a staggering but expected first-quarter loss of $1.11 billion due to the pending sale of its Snapple beverage business, said Wednesday it has formed a committee to find a replacement for its chairman.

Quaker said the results included a one-time charge of $1.14 billion as the result of the sale of Snapple to Triarch Cos. last month. Quaker said when it announced the sale of Snapple that it would take the charge.
The $1.1 billion loss, which equalled $8.15 a share, compared with income of $32.2 million a year earlier.
Excluding the one-time charge, Quaker said it earned 24 cents a share, which was up from 22 cents a share a year earlier and better than market analysts had expected.
Sales declined to $1.20 bilion from $1.22 billion.
Quaker also said it might sell non-core businesses as part of a plan to reduce costs, repurchase shares and focus on its core businesses. It didn't identify what units those might be.

Quaker said its chairman, William D. Smithburg, would continue to run the company while the committee looked for a replacement. Smithburg, 58, has been chairman and chief executive officer for 16 years.
Quaker's stock gained 75 cents to $39 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
